title: approvalPolicy auto-approve parks MCP-using Codex sessions: it maps to Codex on-request, which turns every MCP tool call into an unanswered elicitation
outcome: Keep native Codex on-request for host AutoApprove while TermAl answers permitted tagged routine MCP approvals itself, retaining read-only/write/external guards, genuine interactive questions and explicit recovery of live pending routine prompts.
acceptance: Under host auto-approve, Codex keeps requesting approval (the on-request mapping is kept, not replaced by never), and TermAl itself approves permitted routine MCP tool-call approval requests (elicitations tagged codex_approval_kind mcp_tool_call), so routine calls such as read mailbox, ack, send, spawn and tracker note complete without operator input.

Host guards stay enforced: for read-only delegations TermAl declines non-exempt write or external tool calls exactly as for ordinary approvals; genuine form elicitations, URL elicitations and user-input prompts stay interactive; tests cover each boundary.

Regression coverage through the production paths: session creation and settings mutation with auto-approve and never, and ordinary MCP calls under each, asserting that auto-approve never leaves a routine tool-call prompt for the operator.

A recovery path for sessions already parked on routine mcp_tool_call prompts, needing no human click on each prompt: an explicit operator selection or reselection of host auto-approve resolves that session's live pending routine tool-call prompts per the host policy; genuine questions stay pending; a test covers it.
The maintained full five-stage gate passes on the exact final input, and the independent review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
